Getting started

Your first step beyond.

A straightforward guide from a fresh install to your first connection.

  1. Choose your launcher

    Install CurseForge or a compatible launcher that can import a CurseForge modpack. Sign in with a Minecraft account that owns Java Edition.

    Use the launcher’s official distribution and let it manage the pack’s mod loader.

  2. Install Mythforge

    Open the official pack listing, choose the version required by the server, and install it into a fresh profile.

    Open the modpack download

  3. Set your memory allocation

    Recommended allocated client RAM: 9-10 GB.

    In your launcher’s profile or Minecraft settings, adjust the memory allocation. Leave enough RAM for your operating system and other programs; allocating all available memory can cause launch failures.

  4. Launch the pack once

    Start Mythforge and let the initial setup finish. Use Java 21 for Minecraft 1.21.1; a supported launcher can usually manage this runtime for you.

    Wait until the main menu loads before connecting.

  5. Open Multiplayer

    From Minecraft’s main menu, select Multiplayer, then Add Server.

  6. Meet us at the horizon

    Enter the address below, save the server, and connect. Take a moment to read the community rules.

    Minecraft server address

Troubleshooting ↓

When the journey stalls

A few things to check.

Wrong modpack version

Compare your installed profile version with the server’s required version. Install the matching release into a separate profile rather than manually mixing mod files. Back up local worlds before updates.

Java or launch errors

Use Java 21 and confirm that your launcher is using a 64-bit runtime. Remove custom JVM arguments you do not understand and retry with the launcher’s defaults. Keep the crash report if the problem continues.

Connection errors

Double-check play.mythforge.win, your internet connection, and the pack version. Restart Minecraft. If other players are also unable to connect, check maintenance announcements.

Insufficient RAM or native memory allocation errors

Close memory-heavy applications and check the launcher’s allocation. More allocated RAM is not always better: Java also needs memory outside its heap. If an error says native memory allocation failed, leave more memory available to the system and check that virtual memory is enabled.

Server maintenance

Check announcements before changing your installation. An unavailable status readout is not proof of an outage. Wait for a maintenance update or ask for help in the community channel.

Still need help?

Provide your modpack version, launcher, allocated RAM, and the relevant crash report or latest log. Remove personal information before sharing logs.
